title: Her mother's death (1877)
hookLine: her earliest sharp memory: being lifted to kiss her mother's forehead, and a coffin that seemed very big
tomorrow: her sister became her second mother. then she overheard something.

lines: LIFTED UP FOR ONE LAST KISS.
cards: Earliest memories are strange. Not the big picture, just small, sharp pieces: a doorway, a smell, the height of a table. Thérèse kept one she never lost.
Her father lifts her up to kiss her mother's forehead one last time. She doesn't cry. She doesn't say a word.
Years later, writing as a young nun, she remembers that the coffin seemed very big, and she had to look up at it.

teach.b: First, the sunny start. Thérèse remembers her earliest years as bright: a loving home, a lively, cheerful little girl, and, she admits, a stubborn one. Then the loss.
Her mother died after an illness, and Thérèse writes that she was four and a half. Then the change, the line the rest of the book leans on.
After her mother's death, she says, her happy temperament changed completely. The lively child became timid and oversensitive. A look could make her cry.
Then the choice. After the funeral, Céline threw herself into Marie's arms: you'll be my mother.
Thérèse, not wanting to be left out, ran to Pauline: then Pauline will be my mother.
Notice how she tells it. She doesn't hurry past the grief or turn it straight into a lesson. She lets the loss be real, lets it change her, and says so in plain words.

how: Catholics pray for the dead, at funerals and especially in November, and some turn to Mary as a mother in grief.

games.q: a girl on the kids' team you help coach goes quiet and cries at small things since her mom died last year. what does Thérèse's story suggest?
o: a loss that young can change a child; that's grief, not attitude.
she's being dramatic; tougher coaching will snap her out of it.
if nobody mentions her mom, she'll be back to normal soon.
games.why: Thérèse says losing her mother changed her temperament completely: timid, oversensitive, crying at a look. she names it plainly, without blame.

practice: Close your eyes and hold in mind a child somewhere who has lost a mother, or the child you once were, if that's your story. If you pray, you can ask Mary, whom Catholics honor as a mother, to keep them close.

wordCard.voice: Her mother's death. The loss at four and a half that, in Thérèse's own account, changed her completely.

carryVoice: Carry this: four years old, because grief that comes so young still counts. Take care today.
